_doc: Mining districts outside the reference empire, plus tags that complete the fuel and metal shares. share_of_reference_output is a district's share of the reference civilisation's output of that resource (the empire total that data/world/resources.json gives for the metals), and is how much of the resource a holder of the tile, or a buyer within reach of it, can draw on; it is read by sim/geography/mineral_shares.py and never enters the supply curve of the reference empire (that is share_of_empire_output on the Roman-world rows). Every share here is a temporary_heuristic: no district-level production series exists in the sources named, so each figure is the rough relative abundance the former region table gave, now sited at one named district. A resource counts as tracked when any row of it carries this field. conf describes the location and the source, not the share. No endowment is given where none could be defended.

entries.name: Scania Coalfield
entries.first_worked_source: This entry's own source: worked from the late eighteenth century. Entered as the start of that late part (1770); no size is given (the geological model sizes the district).
entries.source: Skane (Sweden) coal measures around Hoganas and Bjuv, the Nordic region's small coalfield, worked from the late eighteenth century; location from the Geological Survey of Sweden's description of the Rhaetian-Jurassic coal-bearing beds.
entries.contained_basis: Coal supply of the Skane mining fields estimated at about 300 Mt (1914 handbook; a remaining-supply estimate, production before and after not added)
entries.contained_source: Sweden: historical and statistical handbook, Part 2 Industries, 1914, Project Runeberg, https://runeberg.org/sweden14/2/0269.html : "The supply of coal in the mining fields of Skane is estimated at about 300 million tons" (c. 1914)

entries.name: Bergslagen Iron District
entries.source: Bergslagen (Dalarna, Vastmanland, Orebro), the central Swedish ore district whose bloomery iron was smelted from the Iron Age and exported as osmund iron in the Middle Ages.
entries.contained_basis: Stand-in is Grangesberg: more than 150 Mt of iron ore produced to the 1989 closure plus 82.4 Mt reserves at 37.2% Fe; the mined ore is assumed to have the same 37.2% Fe (assumption), so (150 + 82.4) Mt x 0.372 = 86.45 Mt iron
entries.contained_source: Mining Technology, Grangesberg Iron Ore Project, https://www.mining-technology.com/projects/grangesberg-iron-ore-project-sweden/ : the mine "was closed in December 1989 ... after producing more than 150Mt of iron ore"; reserves 82.4Mt (37.2% Fe, July 2022)

entries.name: Sala Lead Mine
entries.first_worked_source: This entry's own source: worked from the fifteenth century at the latest. Entered as the start of that century; no earlier working is attested in the source, and no size is given (the geological model sizes the district).
entries.source: Sala silver-lead mine, Vastmanland, worked from the fifteenth century at the latest; the galena carries the silver. Position from the Swedish national heritage listing of the mine.
entries.contained_basis: About 35,000 tons of lead extracted over the life of the mine (tons taken as metric); no reserves, mine closed 1908, so effectively complete production
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Sala Silver Mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sala_Silver_Mine : "more than 200 million ounces of silver and about 35,000 tons of lead"

entries.name: Sala Silver Mine
entries.source: Sala silver mine, Vastmanland, Sweden's chief silver producer from the late Middle Ages; the same working as the lead entry, listed once per metal.
entries.first_worked_source: The same working as sala_lead, whose source dates it to the fifteenth century at the latest; entered as the start of that century. No size is given (the geological model sizes the district).
entries.contained_basis: More than 200 million troy ounces x 31.1035 g = 6,221 t silver extracted; mine closed 1908
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Sala Silver Mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sala_Silver_Mine : "more than 200 million ounces of silver"

entries.name: Magan Copper (Oman)
entries.source: Wadi Jizzi and Lasail copper of the Semail ophiolite, smelted from the third millennium BC (Magan of the cuneiform texts); Weisgerber's excavations of the Oman copper smelting sites.

entries.name: Mahd adh Dhahab
entries.source: Mahd adh Dhahab ('Cradle of Gold'), Hejaz, an ancient gold, silver and copper working; Luce, O'Neil and Rye, Mahd adh Dhahab: Precambrian epithermal gold deposit in Saudi Arabia, US Geological Survey Open-File Report 78-388 (1978), https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/ofr78388. Silver is a minor product.
entries.working_unknown: UNKNOWN (D): this entry's source note gives the place and a share of reference output, not a working date or a total endowment. Not entered as first_worked or endowment, so the deposit is listed as unworked in the opening stores.
entries.contained_basis: Recorded production 1939 to 1954 of 1,002,029 troy ounces of silver x 31.1035 g = 31.17 t silver (the same period gave 765,768 oz gold); the ancient workings (about 950 BC and 750 to 1258 AD) have no production figure, and no reserve is given, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: USGS Open-File Report 76-865, Geology and ore deposits of the Mahd adh Dhahab district, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1976/0865/report.pdf : "The early production is not known, but the recorded production in 1939-54 is 765,768 fine ounces gold and 1,002,029 ounces silver."

entries.name: Wadi Sawawin Iron
entries.source: Wadi Sawawin banded iron formation, Midyan terrane of northwest Saudi Arabia, about 60 km from the Red Sea port of Duba; the one large iron body of the peninsula. No ancient working is attested, so this share is a placeholder for the peninsula's small iron output. Position approximate (no published coordinate found).
entries.contained_basis: Reserve of 383 Mt of ore at 40% iron = 153.2 Mt iron; London Mining figure of 2013 as quoted by Wikipedia, no production before it
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Wadi Sawawin mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wadi_Sawawin_mine : "an estimated reserve of 383 million tonnes of ore grading 40% iron"

entries.name: Konasamudram Iron (Deccan)
entries.source: Konasamudram and Nirmal (Telangana), the Deccan centre where wootz crucible steel was made from local ores; Craddock on early Indian iron and steel. Share for the subcontinent's iron.

entries.name: Khetri Copper Belt
entries.source: Khetri-Singhana belt, Rajasthan, copper worked since the Ganeshwar-Jodhpura culture (Ganeshwar site, Wikipedia); Willies, Ancient and post-medieval mining sites in the Khetri copper belt and the Kolar gold field, India, Bulletin of the Peak District Mines Historical Society 11(6), 1992, 285-295, listed in the Heritage of Metals and Societies review of Indian metallurgy but not read here. No joint Hegde and Craddock work on Khetri was found.
entries.contained_basis: Sum of four ore-reserve blocks (reserves including resources) of the Khetri belt: Khetri 26 Mt at 1.13% Cu, Kolihan 20.64 Mt at 1.35%, Banwas 25.02 Mt at 1.69%, Chandmari-Kolihan 12.10 Mt at 1.03% = 0.294 + 0.279 + 0.423 + 0.125 = 1.12 Mt copper; no past production added and other belt deposits (Madan Kudhan) not counted, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Hindustan Copper Limited, Khetri Copper Complex, https://www.hindustancopper.com/Page/KCCPlant : "Khetri Mine 26 million tonnes @ 1.13 % Cu; Kolihan Mine 20.64 million tonnes @ 1.35 % Cu; Banwas Block 25.02 million tonnes @ 1.69 % Cu; Chandmari-Kolihan Intervening block 12.10 million tonnes @ 1.03 % Cu"

entries.name: Hazaribagh Tin
entries.source: Cassiterite of the Hazaribagh-Gaya mica belt, Bihar-Jharkhand, as a placeholder for the small Indian tin output. No source found for tin in Hazaribagh or Gaya (Indian Bureau of Mines Bihar listings omit tin; India's commercial cassiterite is in Bastar and Dantewada, Chhattisgarh), so the occurrence is unverified. Ancient India imported most of its tin.

entries.name: Zawar Lead
entries.source: Zawar, Udaipur, Rajasthan: lead-zinc-silver mines with a Mauryan-period phase (radiocarbon on mine timbers, late first millennium BC) and a second phase from the fourteenth century, where medieval zinc distillation was practised; Craddock and Hegde, Early Indian Metallurgy (Zawar, Agucha, Dariba), https://esamskriti.com/e/Culture/Indian-Culture/ZINC-Mining-in-Zawar-region-of-Rajasthan~Interview-with-Dr.-Paul-T.-Craddock-1.aspx.
entries.contained_basis: Reserve of 62.7 Mt at 1.2% lead = 752,400 t lead (Hindustan Zinc, FY2025-26); modern company reserve, ancient and past output not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Hindustan Zinc, Integrated Annual Report FY2025-26, Business Snapshot, https://integratedreport.hzlindia.com/annual-integrated-report-fy-2025-26/business-snapshot.html : "Zawar Mines Udaipur, Rajasthan 103.7 Mnt Resource 62.7 Mnt Reserves Reserve metal grades 2.5% Zinc 1.2% Lead 21 g/MT Silver"

entries.name: Zawar Silver
entries.source: Zawar, Rajasthan: silver from the argentiferous galena, as the lead entry; Craddock and Hegde, Early Indian Metallurgy. Silver recovery here is not independently re-checked.
entries.working_unknown: UNKNOWN (D): this entry's source note gives the place and a share of reference output, not a working date or a total endowment. Not entered as first_worked or endowment, so the deposit is listed as unworked in the opening stores.
entries.contained_basis: Reserve of 62.7 Mt at 21 g/t silver = 1,317 t silver (Hindustan Zinc, FY2025-26); the company does not say whether the silver is recovered; ancient and past output not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Hindustan Zinc, Integrated Annual Report FY2025-26, Business Snapshot, https://integratedreport.hzlindia.com/annual-integrated-report-fy-2025-26/business-snapshot.html : "Zawar Mines Udaipur, Rajasthan 103.7 Mnt Resource 62.7 Mnt Reserves Reserve metal grades 2.5% Zinc 1.2% Lead 21 g/MT Silver"

entries.name: Choghart-Chadormalu Iron
entries.source: Choghart iron oxide deposit, Bafq district (Yazd), about 12 km northeast of Bafq, with Chadormalu 80 km to the north; a large Precambrian iron body. Medieval working is not independently verified.
entries.contained_basis: Choghart only (the neighbour of Chadormalu in the Bafq district): proven resources of 200 Mt at more than 60% Fe = at least 120 Mt iron; Chadormalu itself not counted, so a lower bound for the row
entries.contained_source: JpGU 2008 abstract, Choghart deposit, Bafq, Iran, https://www2.jpgu.org/meeting/2008/program/pdf/K130/K130-017_e.pdf : "The deposit has proven resources of 200 million tons with more than 60 % Fe on average."

entries.name: Anarak Copper
entries.source: Talmessi and Meskani copper-nickel-cobalt ores, Anarak district, Iran; Encyclopaedia Iranica (Copper ii, Copper resources in Iran; Anarak) gives Talmessi as a possible early native-copper mine and Anarak copper mining as probably pre-Islamic, so Bronze Age working here is not confirmed. Kerman's Sar Cheshmeh is the larger modern body.

entries.name: Mushiston Tin
entries.source: Mushiston copper-tin deposit, Kaznok valley of the Zeravshan mountains about 35 km south of Penjikent (Tajikistan), mined from the end of the third millennium BC; Karnab, Lapas and Changali (Uzbekistan) lie farther west and are not covered by this point. Cierny, Weisgerber and Parzinger on Central Asian tin; Frontiers in Earth Science 2023, doi 10.3389/feart.2023.1224873. Position approximate.

entries.name: Karamazar Lead
entries.source: Karamazar range (Kan-i-Mansur), Tajikistan and Uzbekistan: mining and smelting of the ninth to eleventh centuries is attested at the Mansura mine (Wikipedia, Mining in Tajikistan); the geographers' accounts of it were not checked. Position approximate.
entries.contained_basis: Stand-in is Konimansuri Kalon in the Kan-i-Mansur (Karamazar) range: about 1 billion tons of ore at 0.49% lead = 4.9 Mt lead; an estimated possible resource, historic Samanid workings not counted
entries.contained_source: Asia-Plus, Technical issues impede completion of tender for development of Konimansuri Kalon deposit, https://asiaplustj.info/en/news/tajikistan/economic/20120111/technical-issues-impede-completion-tender-development-konimansuri-kalon-deposit : "estimated to contain around 1 billion tons of ore ... around 49 grams of silver, with 0.38 percent zinc and 0.49 percent lead"

entries.name: Karamazar Silver
entries.source: Karamazar range (Kan-i-Mansur): silver mines of the Samanid period, as the lead entry; Transoxianan silver feeding Samanid dirhams is argued in the Journal of Historical Research (jhr.usb.ac.ir/article_9357). Position approximate.
entries.working_unknown: UNKNOWN (D): this entry's source note gives the place and a share of reference output, not a working date or a total endowment. Not entered as first_worked or endowment, so the deposit is listed as unworked in the opening stores.
entries.contained_basis: Stand-in is Konimansuri Kalon in the Kan-i-Mansur (Karamazar) range: possible silver reserves of about 70,000 tons (Micon survey, raised from 57,000 tons); tons taken as metric; historic Samanid output not counted
entries.contained_source: Asia-Plus, Technical issues impede completion of tender for development of Konimansuri Kalon deposit, 11 January 2012, https://asiaplustj.info/en/news/tajikistan/economic/20120111/technical-issues-impede-completion-tender-development-konimansuri-kalon-deposit : "raised its possible silver reserves to some 70,000 tons"

entries.name: Handan-Wu'an Iron
entries.source: Handan-Wu'an (Hebei) skarn iron district; Han state ironworks such as Tieshenggou (Henan, about 200 km southwest) are described in Wagner, Iron and Steel in Ancient China (Brill, 1993), which does not itself source the Handan ore. Ore source is not independently verified.
entries.contained_basis: Handan-Xingtai (Han-Xing) skarn district: more than 100 deposits with proven reserves of about 1 billion tons (ore); iron grade not given by the page, so 40% Fe is assumed (assumption, typical lean skarn magnetite, not sourced) = 400 Mt iron; district-wide stand-in for Wu'an
entries.contained_source: Jin et al., Han-Xing-type skarn iron deposits: insights from trace elements in magmatic magnetite, Frontiers in Earth Science 2025, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/earth-science/articles/10.3389/feart.2025.1567728/pdf : "more than 100 deposits have been discovered, with proven reserves of approximately 1 billion tons"

entries.name: Tonglushan Copper
entries.source: Tonglushan, Daye (Hubei), the best-excavated ancient copper mine in China, worked from the Shang-Zhou period for over a millennium; Hubei Provincial Museum excavation reports.
entries.contained_basis: Ancient slag of about 400,000 metric tons yielding 80,000 to 120,000 t of crude copper; midpoint 100,000 t; production only, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: China Daily, Buried mine rewrites the past (Tonglushan), 16 June 2026, https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202606/16/WS6a3083cfa310986e2b4601cf_2.html : "produced about 400,000 metric tons of ancient slag, yielding between 80,000 and 120,000 tons of crude copper"

entries.name: Gejiu Tin
entries.source: Gejiu (Yunnan): earliest clear working there is copper from the Han period and tin was mined on a large scale only from the early 1900s; long tin exploitation is probable but not proven (Heidelberg Sinology mining project, https://www.zo.uni-heidelberg.de/sinologie/research/epm/09_gejiu.html). Yunnan deposits are reported as China's main Han tin source (Wikipedia, Tin mining).
entries.contained_basis: Predicted tin ore resources of the Gejiu area 2.22 Mt (a prediction; page says 'tin ore resources', taken here as tin metal, unit basis not stated); no production added
entries.contained_source: SMM (Shanghai Metals Market), Dry information: global tin ore distribution, https://news.metal.com/newscontent/100918902-dry-information-throughout-the-global-tin-ore-distribution-development-supply-situation-demand-increases-resources-limit : "the tin ore resources are predicted to be 2.22 million t" (article dated 21 March 2019)

entries.name: Shuikoushan Lead
entries.source: Shuikoushan (Changning, Hunan), a lead-zinc-copper district; Qing-period Hunan lead mining is covered by Lin Rongqin on Hunan mining, but Shuikoushan's own early history was not found. Date of first working unverified.

entries.name: Huize Silver
entries.source: Huize and the Yunnan silver mines: Yunnan was the most productive silver region from the Yuan onward, Ming records name about twenty mines and Qing records about two hundred, and the Jinniu mines at Huize were productive from the late 1780s (Heidelberg Sinology mining project, https://www.zo.uni-heidelberg.de/sinologie/research/epm/12_jinniu_huize.html). Von Glahn, Fountain of Fortune (1996), covers the Ming-Qing silver economy but was not found to treat Huize.
entries.working_unknown: UNKNOWN (D): this entry's source note gives the place and a share of reference output, not a working date or a total endowment. Not entered as first_worked or endowment, so the deposit is listed as unworked in the opening stores.

entries.name: Taruga-Nok Iron
entries.source: Taruga and the Nok culture (central Nigeria), among the earliest iron smelting in West Africa, from the middle of the first millennium BC; Fagg Rackham, Franke, Junius, Maennel and Beck, Early West African Iron Smelting: The Legacy of Taruga in Light of Recent Nok Research, African Archaeological Review (2017), doi 10.1007/s10437-017-9262-2.

entries.name: Akjoujt Copper
entries.source: Akjoujt (Mauritania), copper mined and smelted in the first millennium BC at the Grotte aux Chauves-souris mine (radiocarbon dates reported by Courcier and colleagues, CUPRUM project, citing Lambert 1965 and 1975; Killick 1988 cites Lambert 1971 and 1983 for mid first millennium BC smelting). The title and journal of Lambert 1971 (Les industries sur cuivre dans l'Ouest saharien) were not verified. Medieval working not verified.
entries.contained_basis: Stand-in is the Guelb Moghrein mine at Akjoujt: measured and indicated resource of 43.57 Mt at 0.84% Cu = 364,021 t copper at 31 December 2015; the ancient first-millennium BC workings are not counted and recent production is not added
entries.contained_source: First Quantum Minerals, Guelb Moghrein NI 43-101 technical report, March 2016, https://minedocs.com/12/GuelbMoghrein_Technical_032016.pdf : "Total Measured & Indicated 43.57 0.84 0.69 0.09 364,021 967,184" (Mt, Cu %, Au g/t, As %, Cu t, Au oz)

entries.name: Thai Nguyen Iron
entries.source: Trai Cau and Thai Nguyen iron of northern Vietnam (Geological Survey of Vietnam); iron smelting spread to Dong Son and Oc Eo cultures from the late first millennium BC. Position approximate.

entries.name: Khao Wong Prachan Copper
entries.source: Khao Wong Prachan valley (Lopburi, Thailand), Bronze Age copper mining and smelting; Pigott and Natapintu, Thailand's early copper-base metallurgy.

entries.name: Copperbelt Silver
entries.source: Silver won as a minor by-product of the Central African Copperbelt; no ancient silver mining is attested in the region. The share stands for the region's small silver output.
entries.working_unknown: UNKNOWN (D): this entry's source note gives the place and a share of reference output, not a working date or a total endowment. Not entered as first_worked or endowment, so the deposit is listed as unworked in the opening stores.

entries.name: Nizhny Tagil Iron (Urals)
entries.source: Mount Vysokaya and Gora Blagodat, central Urals, the magnetite behind the Demidov Nizhny Tagil ironworks (begun 1725); Hudson, The Rise of the Demidov Family and the Russian Iron Industry in the Eighteenth Century (Oriental Research Partners, 1986).

entries.name: Gumeshevsk Copper (Urals)
entries.source: Gumeshevskoye (Gumyoshevsky) mine, Polevskoy, Urals: copper in use from the mid second millennium BC (Wikipedia, Gumyoshevsky mine) and a source of Final Bronze Age copper for Itkul and Sarmatian cultures (Ankusheva and colleagues); deposit found 1702, Polevskoy copper smelter 1724 to 1930. Chud and Demidov attributions are not sourced.
entries.contained_basis: Estimated reserves of 48.5 Mt of ore at 1.02% Cu = 494,700 t copper; reserve only (undated), no past production added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Gumyoshevsky mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gumyoshevsky_mine : "estimated reserves of 48.5 million tonnes of ore grading 1.02% copper"

entries.name: Zmeinogorsk Lead (Altai)
entries.source: Zmeinogorsk and the Rudny Altai polymetallic ores, with ancient workings and the Demidov-founded Kolyvan-Voskresensk works (1727); silver ore discovered in winter 1743.
entries.contained_basis: Stand-in is Korbalikhinskoye in the Zmeinogorsky district: reserves of 24.5 Mt of ore at 2.01% lead = 492,450 t lead; reserve only, the Zmeinogorsk mine itself has no figure in any page opened
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Korbalikhinskoye mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korbalikhinskoye_mine : "reserves amounting to 24.5 million tonnes of ore grading 2.01% lead, 9.8% zinc and 43.5 million oz of silver"

entries.name: Zmeinogorsk Silver (Altai)
entries.source: Zmeinogorsk Altai silver, the same ore as the lead entry; first Altai silver was presented in 1744 and the works passed to the Crown for it.
entries.working_unknown: UNKNOWN (D): this entry's source note gives the place and a share of reference output, not a working date or a total endowment. Not entered as first_worked or endowment, so the deposit is listed as unworked in the opening stores.
entries.contained_basis: Stand-in is Korbalikhinskoye in the Zmeinogorsky district: 43.5 million oz of silver x 31.1035 g/oz = 1,353 t silver; reserve only, the Zmeinogorsk mine itself has no figure in any page opened
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Korbalikhinskoye mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korbalikhinskoye_mine : "reserves amounting to 24.5 million tonnes of ore grading 2.01% lead, 9.8% zinc and 43.5 million oz of silver"

entries.name: Cerro de Mercado Iron
entries.source: Cerro de Mercado (Durango), a large hematite-magnetite hill; the pre-Hispanic Americas used iron ore for mirrors and pigment but did not smelt it. The share stands for that small output.
entries.contained_basis: Ore reserve of Cerro Mercado estimated at about 100,000,000 tons (Monterrey steel company estimate, 1920s) times the 65 to 68 per cent iron of the ore as mined (65% used) = 65 Mt iron; tons taken as written; production before 1926 not added
entries.contained_source: William F. Foshag, Mineralogy and geology of Cerro Mercado, Durango, Mexico, Proceedings of the US National Museum (1927), https://archive.org/download/biostor-79733/biostor-79733.pdf : "the ore reserved of Cerro Mercado was approximately 100,000,000 tons"; "The ores as mined contain 65 to 68 per cent of iron"

entries.name: Inguaran Copper (Michoacan)
entries.source: Inguaran, Michoacan, a copper source of West Mexican metallurgy, which began after about AD 700 along the Ecuador-Peru maritime route; Hosler, The Sounds and Colors of Power (MIT Press, 1994) and Hosler and Macfarlane, Copper Sources, Metal Production and Metals Trade in Late Postclassic Mesoamerica, Science 273 (1996) 1819-1824. Inguaran itself is not named in any source found, so its place among the sampled ores is unverified.

entries.name: Taxco Tin
entries.source: Small cassiterite occurrences in the Taxco-Guerrero belt may have supplied tin bronze in prehispanic Mexico (Hosler); not verified. Position approximate.

entries.name: Zimapan Lead
entries.source: Zimapan (Hidalgo), a lead-silver-zinc district worked from the sixteenth century on older native workings.
entries.contained_basis: Two recorded lead figures added: a bonanza of 1793 in the Lomo de Toro mine that yielded 5,700 tons of lead, and 15,000 tons of lead yielded by the district from 1945 to 1949 (tons taken as metric); all other years unrecorded, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: USGS Professional Paper 284, Geology and ore deposits of the Zimapan mining district, State of Hidalgo, Mexico, https://pubs.usgs.gov/pp/0284/report.pdf : "a bonanza struck in the Lomo de Toro mine yielded 5,700 tons of lead"; "from 1945 to 1949 the district probably yielded some 15,000 tons of lead and about the same amount of zinc"

entries.name: Taxco Silver
entries.source: Taxco, Guerrero, early Spanish silver mines of the 1530s (Encyclopedia.com, Taxco; Wikipedia, Taxco gives about 1532) and part of the Mexican silver belt with Zacatecas; Bakewell, Silver Mining and Society in Colonial Mexico: Zacatecas 1546-1700 (Cambridge University Press, 1971) covers Zacatecas, not Taxco.
entries.first_worked_source: This entry's own source: Wikipedia, Taxco, gives about 1532 for the early Spanish silver mines. No size is given (the geological model sizes the district).

entries.name: Oruro-Potosi Tin
entries.source: Oruro and the Bolivian tin belt, a candidate source of Andean tin bronze: tin bronze appears in northern Bolivia in the Tiwanaku period, and Lechtman and Macfarlane's lead isotope work places Tiwanaku bronze ores in the Bolivian puna and high sierra, but no source found names Oruro as the prehispanic tin source. Unverified.
entries.contained_basis: Cerro Rico de Potosi tin reserves 540 Mt ore x 0.17% Sn = 0.918 Mt tin (year not stated); counts Potosi only for this Oruro-Potosi row, production not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Cerro Rico, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerro_Rico : "540 million tons of ore grading 0.17% tin"

entries.name: Cerro de Pasco Lead
entries.source: Cerro de Pasco, Peru, a lead-zinc-silver district worked from the colonial period on pre-Inca workings.

entries.name: Keweenaw Native Copper
entries.source: Keweenaw Peninsula and Isle Royale, Michigan: native copper mined by the Old Copper Complex peoples; lake-sediment geochemistry dates Isle Royale mining to 6500 to 5400 years ago, Pompeani et al., The Holocene (2014), doi 10.1177/0959683614557574.
entries.contained_basis: Around five billion kilograms of copper extracted 1845 to 1968 = 5.0 Mt; production only (other sources give 11 billion lb = 5.0 Mt, and up to 15.5 billion lb through 1996 per a search snippet that was not opened)
entries.contained_source: US National Park Service, Keweenaw industrial landscapes, https://home.nps.gov/articles/000/keweenaw-industrial-landscapes.htm : "Around five billion kilograms of copper were extracted from 1845 to 1968 (Cannon and Nicholson 1)"

entries.name: Mesabi Iron Range
entries.source: Mesabi Range (Minnesota), the Lake Superior taconite and iron ore district that supplied the industrial United States from 1892.
entries.contained_basis: 4.38 Gt of iron ore, concentrates and pellets shipped 1892 to 2008 x assumed 60% Fe average (assumption: natural ore about 50-55% Fe, pellets about 65% Fe, mix not stated) = 2.63 Gt Fe; production only, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources, Historical Perspective, https://dnr.state.mn.us/lands_minerals/mineland_reclamation/historical.html : "From 1892 to 2008, a total of 4.38 billion tons of iron ore, iron ore concentrates and pellets were shipped from the Mesabi Range." (tons taken as the short or long ton the page does not state; not converted)

entries.name: Upper Mississippi Valley Lead
entries.source: Galena-Dubuque lead-zinc district, worked by Native Americans for galena and by Euro-Americans from the 1820s; US Geological Survey.
entries.contained_basis: Total recorded lead production 1798 to 1947 of 814,339 short tons x 0.9072 = 738,770 t lead (the report notes the true total may be nearer 1,000,000 tons); production only
entries.contained_source: USGS Professional Paper 309, The geology of the Upper Mississippi Valley zinc-lead district, 1959, https://pubs.usgs.gov/pp/0309/report.pdf : "The total lead production from 1798 to 1947 was 814,339 short tons of lead metal."

entries.name: Cobalt Native Silver (Ontario)
entries.source: Cobalt-Gowganda district, Ontario, rich native silver found in 1903; native silver also occurs with Keweenaw copper.
entries.working_unknown: UNKNOWN (B): the source gives the discovery (1903) but no endowment was read, so neither a working date nor a size is stated here
entries.contained_basis: Between 405 and 420 million ounces of silver produced by the 1980s; midpoint 412.5 Moz x 31.1035 g = 12,830 t (range 12,600 to 13,060 t); production only
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Cobalt, Ontario, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobalt,_Ontario : "By the 1980s, the area had produced between 405 and 420 million ounces of silver"

entries.name: Burra Copper
entries.source: Burra (South Australia), the first big Australian copper mine, opened 1845; no pre-colonial copper working.
entries.contained_basis: About 50,000 t of copper produced 1845 to 1877; production only
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Burra, South Australia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burra,_South_Australia : the mine produced "approximately 50,000 tonnes of copper" over 1845 to 1877 (as opened by the branch mineral-share-sources, commit 78142b80)

entries.name: Isua Iron Belt (Greenland)
entries.source: Isukasia banded iron formation, southwest Greenland (Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland); the Norse bog-iron working was tiny, hence a small share.
entries.contained_basis: 951 Mt of resource at 36% Fe (cut-off 25% Fe) = 342 Mt iron, as of March 2010; the inferred 837 Mt at 36.4% Fe overlaps and is not added
entries.contained_source: Mining Technology, Isua Iron Ore Project, https://www.mining-technology.com/projects/isua-project/ : "As of March 2010, the mine contained 951Mt at 36% Fe reported at a cut off grade of 25% Fe."

entries.name: Bihar-Bengal Saltpetre Earths
entries.source: Saran, Tirhut and Patna districts on the Gangetic plain: potassium nitrate leached from efflorescent soils, the world's main saltpetre supply from the 1600s; Buchanan, Hamilton and East India Company records.

entries.name: Iranian Nitre Earths
entries.source: Nitre earths of the Iranian plateau (Khorasan, Kerman, Yazd) leached for saltpetre in the Safavid period. Position approximate.

entries.name: Shanxi Nitre Earths
entries.source: Chinese xiao shi was gathered from nitre earths in north China (Shanxi, Shaanxi) and Sichuan; Needham, Science and Civilisation in China vol 5, part 7. Position approximate.
